lesson_title: It Works. So Why Is It a Failure?
hook_text: A stove that cooks perfectly and burns down homes. A chair that seats everyone and ends up in a landfill. Working is not enough.
clip_script: Three objects. A hydraulic rescue spreader, a plastic school chair, a paraffin stove. All three work. Are they fit for purpose? Eight questions decide. Users: who uses it? Purpose: why does it exist? Function: does it do the job? Cost-effectiveness: is it good value, not just cheap? The spreader costs more than a car and is still a bargain, because it saves lives for thirty years. Safety: can it hurt anyone? Here the stove fails: open flame, fuel tank, tips over, thousands of burns a year. Ergonomics: does it fit the body? Aesthetics: does it look right? Red paint helps a rescuer find the tool in the dark. Impact on society and the environment: who else pays? The chair sits in a landfill for centuries; the stove fills a room with smoke. Working is the start. Fit for purpose is all eight at once. Now go and check your own rescue device against every one.
visual_style: Whiteboard row of three objects with eight tick-or-cross columns filling in beneath them; the stove's safety and impact cells turn red.
mood: Thoughtful and a little sobering, ending on a practical checklist.
pacing: Three objects in three seconds, then one beat per question, slow on the stove's failures.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and add the eight considerations to your design brief.
